To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(a) The effects of CO2 enrichment on forest ecosystems are likely to depend on the species composition of the forest.
the effects of increased atmospheric CO2 concentrations on the productivity of a forest ecosystem will be less than the effects on the growth of individual trees.

1) the increase in biomass of a stand is less than the increase in growth rate of individual trees, 2) the increase in growth of a stand depends on the species composition and age of the stand and 3) the effects on the stand are more pronounced when the stand is young than when it is mature.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of increased CO2 concentration on the productivity and composition of forests.
the following questions: (1) How does CO2 enrichment affect plant growth, and how can this be quantified?

the following questions: 1) What is the response of the growth of forest ecosystems to increased CO2 concentrations? 2) What are the implications for the structure of the ecosystem? 3) How do these implications affect ecosystem function? 4) What are the effects of increased CO2 on the productivity of forest ecosystems?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
we cannot predict with any certainty the effects of increased atmospheric CO2 on forests.
the effects of CO2 enrichment on forests is not known.
the effects of increased atmospheric CO2 on forest productivity are uncertain and depend on the specific forest type, the climate and the management.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the effects of CO2 on the growth of individual trees are not sufficient to explain the observed increase in productivity of many ecosystems.
there is a need for a more complete understanding of the effects of CO2 enrichment at the ecosystem level.
we do not know what to expect from the effects of increased CO2 on forests.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the effects on the ecosystem are likely to be less than the effects on the individual tree.
ecosystem level effects of CO2 on forests are likely to be much smaller than the responses of the component trees.
the ecosystem level response to CO2 is likely to be a function of both the response at the individual plant level and the structure of the ecosystem.
